# Lives of Scripture

> A reference for every person named in the Bible — who they were, how they
> connect by genealogy and relationship, and what their story reveals about
> God's redemptive plan. Content is grounded in the biblical text itself
> (NASB as the base translation, KJV name-spelling selectable), not
> Wikipedia, and is written from a conservative evangelical (Open Brethren /
> Plymouth Brethren) theological perspective. No verse text is quoted
> anywhere on the site for copyright reasons — citations are
> book/chapter/verse references only.

## Content model

- Two tiers: "full" entries (~700 narratively-documented figures) carry a
  story, a devotional reflection, genealogy, and an image. "Stub" entries
  (~2,250 names) are single-reference genealogy/list mentions with no
  narrative to tell — they exist to keep the genealogy graph complete, not
  as standalone articles, and are marked `noindex` accordingly.
- Every person page states its sources as Scripture references
  (book:chapter:verse), never inventing narrative content beyond what the
  text states. Disputed identifications, dating, and authorship questions
  are labeled as disputed rather than resolved silently.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://livesofscripture.org/): overview, featured person, and quiz question.
- [People](https://livesofscripture.org/people.html): searchable/filterable index of every named person.
- [Timeline](https://livesofscripture.org/timeline.html): chronological view across biblical eras.
- [Connections](https://livesofscripture.org/connections.html): genealogy and narrative-relationship graph between people.
- [Place Connections](https://livesofscripture.org/place-connections.html): graph pairing each named place with the people Scripture ties to it.
- [Churches](https://livesofscripture.org/churches.html): every New Testament church and the people Scripture ties to it by name.
- [Places](https://livesofscripture.org/places.html): every named biblical place with a documented connection to a person's story, cross-linked to the people found there and, where relevant, noting whether its modern-day identification is confirmed, traditional, or disputed.
- [Map explorer](https://livesofscripture.org/map.html): free, copyright-free, customizable maps of the biblical world. The site draws its own label-free base maps from public-domain Natural Earth geometry (no slippy tiles, no modern country labels or borders), plots places from OpenBible.info coordinates, and offers preset groups (the Exodus route, Paul's journeys, the seven churches of Revelation, and more). Every map is free to reuse with no copyright claimed and no attribution required, and the page offers the blank base maps (parchment, plain, and shaded-relief terrain, two extents) as direct SVG/JPEG downloads. Each place page also carries a static locator map generated the same way.
- [Charts](https://livesofscripture.org/charts.html): kings & prophets timeline, the two genealogies of Jesus, the twelve tribes, and chapter-by-chapter charts of Genesis, Job, and Acts.
- [Quiz](https://livesofscripture.org/quiz.html): a printable Bible-knowledge quiz builder.
- [About](https://livesofscripture.org/about.html): sourcing, translation handling, and methodology.
- [Sitemap](https://livesofscripture.org/sitemap.xml): full URL list (full-tier person pages, church pages, full-tier place pages, and site pages; stub person/place pages are intentionally excluded — see Content model above).

## Sourcing

- Primary source: the biblical text itself (NASB).
- Background/context: Easton's Bible Dictionary, Smith's Bible Dictionary, ISBE, Hitchcock's Bible Names Dictionary (all public domain).
- Genealogy data: [BradyStephenson/bible-data](https://github.com/bradystephenson/bible-data) (CC BY 4.0).
- Map base geometry: [Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/) (public domain). Place coordinates and identification confidence: [OpenBible.info](https://www.openbible.info/geo/) (CC BY 4.0). The rendered maps themselves carry no copyright claim.
